en.headline: Police warn of AI voice scams after 150 WhatsApp hijackings cause HK$26 million losses
en.dek: In the past two weeks scammers have used artificial intelligence to imitate the voices of hijacked account holders’ relatives; one victim lost HK$10 million.
body: Hong Kong police recorded 150 WhatsApp account hijacking cases in the past two weeks, with total losses exceeding HK$26 million, according to a Cyberdefender platform alert issued on Wednesday.

In one case a victim was scammed out of HK$10 million after fraudsters impersonated his father. Scammers sent a voice message claiming an urgent need to transfer money and continued making demands until the savings were depleted.

The force warned that after compromising an account, fraudsters may use artificial intelligence to fake the voices of people close to the victim. Residents were advised not to trust voice messages blindly, even if the voice sounds familiar, and to call the person directly to verify identity before making any transfer.
Police also urged the public to enable two-factor authentication and regularly review the devices linked to their messaging accounts.

zh.headline: 警誡WhatsApp被盜用後AI語音詐騙 兩周150宗損失逾2600萬
zh.dek: 騙徒在過去兩周利用人工智能模仿被盜帳戶親友聲音，其中一宗受害人損失1000萬元。
body: 香港警方「網絡守護者」平台星期三發出警示，過去兩周錄得150宗WhatsApp帳戶被盜用個案，總損失超過2600萬元。
其中一宗個案中，受害人被騙徒冒充其父親，損失1000萬元。騙徒先發送語音訊息聲稱急需轉帳，其後繼續提出要求，直至儲蓄耗盡。
警方警告，騙徒在盜用帳戶後，可能使用人工智能模仿受害人親友的聲音。市民不應盲目相信語音訊息，即使聲音相似亦不一定屬實，應先致電有關人士核實身份才進行任何轉帳。
警方亦呼籲市民啟用雙重認證，並定期檢查連結至訊息帳戶的裝置。
